notes:
Need to search first.I couldn't write any notes on Job 29, because I didn't manage to read a single source page.

My first try went straight to the commentary pages (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary and Gill on BibleHub, Precept Austin and the NET Bible notes). The tool turned every request down, because it only opens pages that have first come up in a search. When I then tried to run the searches, the tool told me I had no more research calls left for this turn.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to leave out anything I couldn't find, so there's nothing I can honestly include. I haven't filled any verses in from memory.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll search first and then read the pages. I'd start with these:
- **Verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word on Job 29, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Barnes on BibleHub or StudyLight, Matthew Henry, and Precept Austin's Job 29 page.
- **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Spurgeon on spurgeon.org, and anything on Job's past goodness and self-righteousness from Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, Desiring God or GTY.
- **Other views:** the NET Bible notes on verses 4, 6, 18 and 20, Bible Odyssey on Job, and Catholic, Orthodox or Church Fathers material on Job 29 from New Advent and CCEL (for example, Gregory the Great's *Moralia*).
